title: Acquire Falisse and both Tan studies from AddBiomechanics with metadata reconstruction

decision_context.note: José: make sure we can reconstruct the metadata columns.

summary: Headers only (15 of 36 B3D files: all 11 Falisse, 2 Tan running, 2 Tan walking; 88 MB, no frame bytes). Reconstructable from the B3D header or archive path for all three: subject, recording and observation identity (segment), both reference sides, observation type (continuous_recording), mass, height, sex, age, 'healthy' tag, per-trial timestep, model, force-plate count and per-frame GRF flags. task_id comes from trial names. Missing (left missing, never filled): speed for all three, incline for all three, source clock offsets; Tan running speed values and strike-pattern/footwear meaning of the tokens (abstract only; full text needs library access); Tan walking per-segment speed and modification level (one AddBiomechanics trial per modification versus 9 protocol trials). Two new findings: (1) Falisse: exactly one of the 35 four-man/four-woman subsets of the 11 AddBiomechanics subjects (subjects 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10) reproduces all six TBME 2017 cohort statistics (age 29.8 ± 3.9 y, height 176 ± 6.6 cm, mass 69.6 ± 6.0 kg), so the folder is very likely the paper's 8 volunteers plus 3 extra men (subjects 1, 7, 8); still unresolved are those 3 and the trials (Gait/STS/StairUp versus the paper's six motions), so Falisse task and protocol facts stay unresolved; (2) the dynamics-pass model total mass differs from the entered mass (Falisse 0.71x to 1.80x; one subject 118.0 versus 65.5 kg; Tan 1.00x to 1.09x), a normalization-mass convention for the later mapping step. All trials read have passes kinematics, lowPassFilter, dynamics; legacy index 1 is the low-pass pass. Proposed one row per frame from the dynamics pass: D-HIST-04-1. 36 plan-only acquisition specs (archive zip member route, stream-inflate, CRC32 + SHA-256, Drive header hash cross-check) pass validate_spec in-process; acquisition script not written (placeholder hash); nothing launched. Transient disk is one expanded B3D at a time, up to 2.22 GB (6 of 8 Tan running files exceed 2.0 GB); D-HIST-03-1's 'under 2 GB' used the compressed size.
checks: Drive tree: six No_Arm folders (train/test for Falisse2017, Tan2021, Tan2022) listed from public pages: 36 B3D files, same 36 member paths as the archive central directory (sha256 88d494cc...ce09, verified in the builder).

Header fetch: per file bytes 0-7 then one single-range request for the header (206 each). Header length 3.17-19.87 MB. Every receipt records Content-Range and header SHA-256; the builder re-hashes the saved bytes.
Layout: 8 + header + sum(trial length x (sensor frame + passes x pass frame)) equals the file size for 15 of 15; Drive file size equals archive expanded size for 15 of 15.

Fields absent in every trial header: trial_type, trial_tag, detected_trial_feature, original start/end frame and time, marker_names_guessed; data_quality absent in every header. These are reported as absent, not as proto3 defaults (treadmill/pilotData).
Falisse paper text: KU Leuven accepted manuscript (pypdf extraction), section II.A quotes in audit publications.fa16.

Tan running: PubMed abstract only (E-utilities); paper-fetch (Unpaywall, publisher) and SSRN failed. Tan walking: TII abstract (Semantic Scholar), author README, and a 2025 PLOS One article describing the same 17-subject dataset (secondary; protocol quotes re-checked in saved HTML).
Masses: <mass> of the 14 bodies in each pass's model text; kinematics-model sum = entered mass + 0.13 kg in all 15; dynamics-model sum differs (audit mass_check).

Specs: 36 written, guarded_launcher.validate_spec passed in-process for each; 3600 s timeout, 256 MiB address space, PM-01 memory reserves, disk floor 15 GiB + 2x expanded size on /mnt/s/locomotion_data (free about 153 GiB), receipts outside output roots. Not launched.

Sheets built with common/review_sheet.py from the committed builder; rendered at 1280 px and at 390 px (via a 390 px iframe because headless Chrome's minimum viewport is 500 px); phone layout stacks chips, figures and the options table without clipping.

Rework 2026-10-31 (HIST-04-verify.json round 1): subset test reproduced in the builder (falisse_subsets): 35 subsets, one 6/6 match (subjects 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9, 10), next best 3/6. Mass-ratio range recomputed from the audit (Falisse 0.706-1.801). No new downloads.

decisions.question: Each AddBiomechanics frame holds the raw sensor data plus three processed versions of the motion (marker fit, filtered, and force-matched). The current converter writes all four as separate rows. How many rows per frame should LocoHub write for Falisse and both Tan studies?

options.label: One row per frame from the force-matched (dynamics) result
options.consequence: About 3.7 million rows (about 4 GB before compression); the other two versions, raw markers and raw plate readings are left out. Each file is deleted after conversion, so they return only by re-downloading from the archive while it serves the same hash-checked bytes and reconverting. Values will differ from the old files, which used the filtered version.

options.label: One row per frame for each of the three processed versions
options.consequence: About 11.0 million rows (about 11 GB before compression) with a version column users must filter on; raw markers and plate readings left out. Reversible.

options.label: Keep the current converter: raw row plus one row per version
options.consequence: About 14.6 million rows, every field stored as text; nothing left out; size not estimated; no converter change. Reversible.

decisions.options_order: By row count: about 3.7, 11.0 and 14.6 million.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Acquisition can still be planned and piloted; conversion of the three studies waits; their pages stay legacy; no active dataset is affected.
decisions.why: A follows José's preference for fewer rows, keeps every frame with its force-quality flag, and uses AddBiomechanics' final force-matched result. Left-out data can be rebuilt only by re-downloading from the archive while it serves the same hash-checked bytes and reconverting. Cost: values will not match the old files, and a separate convention is still needed for which body mass normalizes moments.
decisions.check: Decision sheet figure: option C's bar (14.6 million rows) is four times option A's (3.7 million).

decisions.question: Eight of the eleven AddBiomechanics Falisse participants very likely are the volunteers of the cited 2017 paper, but three extra men are unexplained, and the files hold only 3 of the paper's 6 motions (gait, sit-to-stand, stair ascent; squat, stair descent and squat jump are absent). Should LocoHub contact the AddBiomechanics team or the KU Leuven authors to ask which participants are the paper's volunteers, who the other three are, and which protocol the trials followed?

options.label: No, do not contact
options.consequence: Falisse stays unreleasable with task and protocol unresolved; acquisition and demographics are unaffected; no outward contact. Reversible.

options.label: Yes, contact them
options.consequence: One email from José; if answered, Falisse task, protocol and citation could be resolved for all eleven; no data or download change. Reversible until sent.

decisions.options_order: By outward action: none, then one email.
decisions.cost_of_waiting: Falisse stays unreleasable; Tan running and Tan walking are unaffected; acquisition can proceed.
decisions.why: Only the source team can confirm the trial protocol and the three extra participants; without it the Falisse task mapping cannot be sourced, and the request costs one email.
decisions.check: HIST-04 sheet figure: exactly one subset (blue bar at 6) reproduces all six statistics the paper reports.
